items.title: BIG TECH = BANKING ON BIG AI BETS = DRIVING UP INTEREST RATES.
items.content:
BIG TECH = BANKING ON BIG AI BETS = DRIVING UP INTEREST RATES.
 x.com/Hedgeye/status/2098751… Hedgeye (@Hedgeye)Hyperscaler debt is soaring:

Amazon  $AMZN , Alphabet  $GOOGL , Microsoft  $MSFT and Meta  $META have sold over $200 billion of bonds so far in 2026, a record that more than doubles last year's $78 billion.

The pace has accelerated sharply from the prior decade, when the four rarely issued more than $30 billion combined in a full year.

The debt is funding a surge in AI infrastructure spending, from data centers to chips, and 2026 is only year to date.

Combined capex guidance for the four now runs near $700 billion this year. 

Cash flow no longer covers it, Amazon's spending ran to 102% of operating cash flow over the trailing year.

The buildout now runs near 2% of U.S. GDP, and by some estimates accounts for about a third of this year's growth.

The debt is how they're funding it.—  https://x.com/Hedgeye/status/2098751480345825639 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Sep 12, 2026

items.title: HOUSING AFFORDABILITY = TRUMP’S ACHILLES HEEL.
items.content:
HOUSING AFFORDABILITY = TRUMP’S ACHILLES HEEL.
 x.com/kobeissiletter/status/… The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter)US housing affordability is rapidly deteriorating:

The annual income needed to afford an average home in the US surged +$4,107 in May, to a record $124,674 per year.

This marks the 3rd consecutive monthly increase, totaling +$9,734.

By comparison, US median household income stands at $86,159 per year.

This brings the gap between median household income and the income needed to afford an average home to $38,515, the largest gap since July 2025.

This is just $2,288 below the $40,803 record set in June 2024.

To put this into perspective, median household income was $5,139 higher than the income required to buy a home in 2021.

Homeownership is becoming increasingly out of reach for the average American.—  https://x.com/KobeissiLetter/status/2098449646930600177 
— Steve Hanke (@steve_hanke) Sep 12, 2026
